questions.question: Which command prints every line of app.conf that is NOT a comment starting with #?
questions.explanation: -v inverts the match, printing lines that do not match the pattern. -c only counts and -o prints just the matched text.

questions.question: Why does `grep "orders/4." access.log` match a line containing "orders/42"?
options: In a regular expression, . matches any single character
grep ignores everything after a slash
The pattern is treated as a prefix match on file names
questions.explanation: The dot is a regex metacharacter meaning any character, so 4. matches 42. Use grep -F to search for a literal dot.

questions.question: In a script, `grep -q "error" app.log` finds no matching lines. What exit status does it return?
questions.explanation: grep exits 0 when at least one line matches, 1 when no lines match and 2 on an error such as a missing file.

questions.question: Which grep invocation lets you write `(4|5)[0-9]{2}` without backslashes, treating |, () and {} as regex operators?
questions.explanation: -E enables extended regular expressions (ERE), where +, ?, |, () and {} are operators. In the default basic syntax they must be backslash-escaped, and -F disables regex entirely.
